Watching a comet from a dark field — Nebula

g.text: Watching a comet from a dark field
By the Field Notes editors · 6 min read
A comet is easiest to find in the hour after dusk, low in the west, a faint smudge with a
tail that points away from the Sun. Binoculars help more than a telescope: the wide field
shows the whole tail at once. Give your eyes twenty minutes to adapt before you look.
Figure 1. The tail points away from the Sun.
Most comets fade within weeks. Check the sky chart for its position each
night: it drifts a little against the stars.

Sleeping tabs, the tab limit, active-first loading, session restore
Up to 16 tabs; past 8, the least recently used sleep. One live connection
per process (browser network ABI 1.0) is shared: the active tab goes first.
